The board is dominated by one event: `fed-decision-in-december` is the top economics event for 42 of the 54 screened accounts that traded economics at all.

Chosen (seven from the board, one found from the tapes):
- perfectnostalgia: 890 markets, 27K fills, positive 28 of 32 months, 66% economics.
- GoldmanSachs (0x71dd2d53…): 100% economics (Fed path), three positive months.
- ATCapital: 99.9% economics, 3,342 fills in 30 days, half maker.
- Ahpo: 3,292 markets, 16 positive months of 16, 42% economics.
- 0x831449c4…: 617 markets in six weeks, 56 economics markets (international CPI/GDP).
- Stonktrader: trades the US CPI bucket markets directly.
- jozeslemsek: $3 fills, 1,017 markets, nine positive months of nine; the only one at our capital scale.

wallets.name: perfectnostalgia
wallets.numbers: All time: kept $181,889 on $2.04M volume (8.9%), rebates 3%, positive 28 of 32 months; last three months $10.7K, $12.7K, $11.7K. 88 days: 2,960 fills, 158 markets (134 economics, 77% of turnover), API kept $35.0K. Economics net on 105 resolved markets $17,992 (8.4% of turnover, t by market 1.55). Taker buys +12.4c per share (t 2.34, 69 markets); maker buys +5.1c (t 0.72). Position cost median $317, p90 $3.2K, max $34.4K; 13-25 economics markets a week.
wallets.mechanism: Positions before the release and holds. Buys the CPI bucket or central-bank outcome it expects, days to weeks ahead, with resting bids plus occasional takes; 76% of bought dollars are held to resolution or still open, the rest is sold at 0.97-0.98 shortly before the event. It often buys two adjacent buckets and loses single markets outright.
wallets.time_gap: None. This is a model edge (which bucket, which decision). First buy is a median 15.6 days before the scheduled end. It has zero taker fills after any of 82 releases, and its resting bids were hit 9 times in the first 60 s after a release for -$1,587.
wallets.evidence: 16 market stories. ECB October no change: Yes at 0.83-0.92 over six weeks, $34.4K, +$5,187. BoE November +25 bps: in at 0.36-0.61 in September, out at 0.983 a week before the meeting, +$2,732. August CPI 3.4%: bids at 0.43-0.47 for ten days, last fill 18 minutes before the release, +$4,356. September CPI: 3.7% +$4,303, 3.6% -$3,240, core m/m 0.2% -$2,442. Timing test on 82 release markets: 149 taker fills more than a day before, $65.5K, edge +$16,603. Falsification: a blind buyer of 0.70-0.90 favourites in the same 53 events earns about zero (-3.2c, -0.1c, -2.7c per share at 7 d, 1 d, 1 h), so the edge is selection.
wallets.replicability: No speed or tooling needed and it works at $50 a position, but the forecast is the whole edge and its inputs are not visible in the data (I did not pull nowcasts or futures-implied odds). Fee: 0.01 rate now, taker on 64% of volume; real charges implied about 0.04 before 11-21. Room: CPI bucket events trade $35-275K each, central-bank events $0.2-1.5M. Risk: a wrong bucket loses the whole stake; July 2026 was -$6.9K.

wallets.name: GoldmanSachs
wallets.numbers: All time kept $86,646. Months: Sep $0.4K, Oct $6.5K, Nov $14.1K; before August under $1.1K a month. 88 days: 246 fills, 23 markets, $267.8K turnover, API kept $21.0K. 72% of buys sold before resolution, FIFO +$14,434, dollar-weighted median hold 45 h. Only 4 markets resolved in the window.
wallets.mechanism: Discretionary swing trading of the Fed-path markets (decision, number of hikes, sequences), in and out several times per market, almost never held to settlement.
wallets.time_gap: None measurable. 33.5% of its Fed-market dollars trade within 6 h after a US data release (5.7% expected by chance), but only two taker fills fall within 120 s. It trades the hours around data, not the seconds.
wallets.evidence: 12 market stories. On 11-10 at 09:02 UTC it bought 111,222 shares of hike 50 bps in December at 0.009 ($1,000), 4.5 hours before CPI, and sold from 13:33 at 0.096 for +$9.7K: two thirds of the month. On 10-28 at 18:02, two minutes after the FOMC statement, it bought hike 25 bps in December at 0.81-0.82, cut it at 0.64 on 11-05, rebought at 0.65 and 0.83. Fed October no change: five round trips between 0.43 and 0.93, exit at 0.971 ten minutes before the statement.
wallets.replicability: Not mechanically copyable: judgement about the Fed path, positions of $1-77K. Fee 0.01 now; its real charges implied 0.048 before 11-21. Room is large (the December event has traded over $50M). Risk: one ticket carries the quarter.

wallets.name: ATCapital
wallets.numbers: Joined 2026-10-03. Kept $28,640, 14% of it rebates and rewards. October $1.3K, November $26.5K, last 14 days -$2.4K. 88 days: 3,468 fills in 23 markets, $2.12M turnover, 53% maker; 62 merges, 11 neg-risk conversions, 2 splits. About $1.0M of inventory at cost is still open.
wallets.mechanism: Two-sided quoting across the outcomes of the December Fed event, building and merging sets, plus large No positions at 0.990-0.999 on the cut outcomes ($40K lots) and neg-risk conversions.
wallets.time_gap: None; market making and balance-sheet use. It has 23 taker fills within 120 s of a US release, all $11-440: quote maintenance.

wallets.replicability: Not at our scale: about $1M of inventory and continuous quoting. Fee: maker on half the volume; taker rate 0.0102 after 11-21 by its own charges. Two months and one event: persistence unknown.

wallets.name: Ahpo
wallets.numbers: All time kept $154,896 on $15.8M volume (0.98%); 16 positive months of 16; last three $21.5K, $8.6K, $12.9K; rebates 4% all time, 11% in November. 88 days: 46,851 fills (about 40K are one maker ladder at 0.85-0.95 in September), 353 markets, $2.0M, 62% maker; economics 79 markets, $898K; API kept $43.0K. Economics FIFO: 86% of buys sold before resolution, +$26,218, dollar-weighted median hold 0.9 h.
wallets.mechanism: Fast, news-reactive trading and quoting in Fed-path markets: takes size in the seconds to minutes after jobs data or the FOMC statement, then sells into the move; otherwise quotes both sides.
wallets.time_gap: Partly: US data release to Fed-market repricing, which is over in about 30 s. 30.3% of its Fed-market dollars trade within 6 h after a US release (5.7% by chance); three taker fills within 60 s for $37K.
wallets.evidence: 12 market stories. 09-04 12:30 (jobs): took 27,343 hike 25 bps in September at 0.432, sold over the next week at 0.54-0.83. 09-16 18:00 (FOMC): took 12,770 hike in October at 0.347, sold at 0.386 inside the hour. 11-06 13:30:19: took $17.0K of hike in December at 0.778, sold $20.0K at 0.790 twenty seconds later. On that same release the first-8-second takers in the two December markets made +$893 on $11.8K marked an hour later, and the 8-33 s takers +$51 on $90K. Only 16 economics markets resolved in the window, so the economics result rests on round trips.
wallets.replicability: Needs positions of $10-57K, a live reading of the data surprise and its direction for the Fed, and order placement within seconds. Edge is about 1% of volume. Fee 0.01. Room: the Fed markets are the deepest in the category. Risk: direction is ambiguous on most releases (CPI, PPI, PCE and ISM days showed no usable move in November).

wallets.name: Stonktrader
wallets.numbers: Kept $98,410. Months May-Nov: $10.1K, $1.8K, $14.8K, -$0.3K, $10.4K, $59.6K, $2.1K. 88 days: 456 fills, 189 markets, $395K; economics is 16 markets and $35K, +$3,465 on 4 resolved. Crypto +$49.9K on 6 markets, tech +$33.2K on 12, politics -$34.9K.

wallets.replicability: Nothing systematic to copy in this category. Studied and set aside.

wallets.name: jozeslemsek
wallets.numbers: All time kept $6,714 on $52.7K volume (12.7%); rebates and rewards 9%. Nine positive months of nine: $25, $188, $20, $143, $161, $370, $664, $1,378, $3,765. 88 days: 18,529 fills, 575 markets (115 economics, 35% of turnover), $41.6K turnover, 88% maker, API kept $5.8K. FIFO round trips: 12,283 lots, cost $15,329, profit $6,422 (42% of cost). Position per market median $4, p90 $205, max $1,157.
wallets.mechanism: Dealer in sub-cent tails. Rests bids at 0.001-0.03 on long-shot outcomes (Fed cut, other central banks, largest-company markets), resells the same shares at 1.5-3x through resting offers days later. Median buy price 0.003; 90% of buys and 88% of sells are maker; median hold 105 h.
wallets.time_gap: None; market making where one tick is 10-30% of the price. No taker activity around releases.
wallets.evidence: 10 market stories. Fed cuts 25 bps in January: 4,487 bought at 0.012, sold at 0.014-0.016 a week later, another 24,599 sold at 0.024. No change in December Yes: bought at 0.017-0.022 and sold at 0.031-0.037 the next day, three times in four days. Cut 50 bps in December: bought at 0.006, 45,000 sold at 0.003, a loss. Falsification of the few-lucky-jumps reading: 302 of 373 markets positive and 54% of profit from the 1.5-3x resale band, but the top ten markets are still 54% of profit. Unsold inventory at cost $4,022.
wallets.replicability: The only one at our scale: $200-4,000 of inventory, resting orders, no speed, no data feed, zero maker fee, plus small liquidity rewards. Room is small: one account earns $1.4-3.8K a month on $16-21K of volume. Untested: whether a second account in the same queues gets filled. Risks: inventory expiring worthless and thin, concentrated profit.

wallets.name: TheElement115 (with road2million)
wallets.numbers: TheElement115: joined 2026-07-21, 151 fills all time, kept $8,491 on $77K volume (11%), no rebates; months Jul-Nov $0.9K, $0.9K, $0.7K, $4.9K, $1.1K. 88 days: 76 fills, all taker buys, $66.3K. In the 53 sampled events: 51 fills in 33 events, $47.7K, edge to final +$4,618, median price paid 0.94, median $401 a fill, max $5,000. road2million (0x0594680e…): kept $5,291 all time, 45 fills, $17.1K, +$3,010.
wallets.mechanism: Release sniping. A taker buy of the outcome the just-published number determines, on bucket markets for CPI, jobs, PCE, PPI, ISM, GDP and central-bank decisions worldwide, then held about two hours to resolution.
wallets.time_gap: Scheduled release to Polymarket repricing: lag 2-18 s in block time, median 7 s, p90 17 s. By source, the first print at 0.95+ comes 2-3 s after ISM, 3 s after StatCan, 4-5 s after ONS, 4-6 s after the FOMC, 6-9 s after BLS and BEA. Across all takers in 53 events, $20.8K was taken on $69.7K; 78% within 15 s, 98.8% within 60 s.
wallets.evidence: Every one of its 76 fills is 2-40 s after a scheduled release; 51 of 51 sampled fills come after the scheduled second, none before. The 25 outside the sample follow the same pattern: Bank of Russia 10:30:05, Copom 21:31:40, China CPI 01:30:16, JOLTS 15:00:04, Michigan sentiment 15:00:02. road2million fills land in the same events at the same block times, so it is the same operator or the same software. October is 58% of TheElement115's profit.
wallets.replicability: Needs the number within 1-3 s of publication, a prepared map from number to bucket, and an order in the book 2-8 s after the release. Capital $300-5,000, recycled in about two hours. Fee 0.01 now; real charges implied 0.036 before 11-21. Room: about $7K a month for all snipers together in the sampled events, with four wallets taking 59%. Not checked: how they get the number and what depth was available beyond what traded. Risks: parsing the wrong figure, several bots ahead, and the lower fee inviting more.

analysis.patterns:
- There are three separate games in this category: seconds after the number (small specialised bots), days before the number (a forecast), and the Fed-path markets (capital and judgement). The leaderboard shows only the last two; the release snipers earn $1-5K a month and never appear on it.
- A time gap exists and it is 2-20 seconds. In 53 scheduled-release events (Sep-Nov 2026) there were 263 taker fills on the winning side below 0.95 after the release: $69.7K notional, $20.8K profit. Under 6 s: $4.5K; 6-15 s: $11.8K; 15-60 s: $4.3K; after one minute: $257 in three months.
- None of the seven leaderboard accounts took a taker fill in the 60 s after the release of a market it traded. The ones that had resting quotes there lost on them.
- Buying the favourite is not an edge by itself: prices 7 days, 1 day and 1 hour before the release are roughly calibrated (0.70-0.90 bucket: -3.2c, -0.1c, -2.7c per share after fee). The winners who position early select.
- Carry after the release does not exist here: markets resolve about two hours after the number. The single exception (October CPI annual and core YoY, resolved ten days late) paid 2.6% on $25.7K.
- Rebates do not matter (0-14% of what was kept) and nobody is in a volume tier. Directional winners buy between 0.30 and 0.97; almost nothing above 0.97 except one balance-sheet account.
- Profits are lumpy: one surprise (core CPI m/m September, $6.7K of the $20.8K pool) or one ticket (GoldmanSachs on 11-10) is a large part of a quarter.
- The category is concentrated: the December Fed event is the top economics event for 42 of the 54 screened accounts that traded economics. Data-release bucket events are small ($35-275K each).
- The economics taker fee was about 0.036-0.048 by real charges before 2026-11-21 and is 0.010 now, so taker strategies here just became cheaper and will likely attract more competition.
- This is a description of three months, not a backtest: 53 events, 419 market tapes, 163K fills. Release times are the standard calendar, accepted where the tape shows the burst.

ideas_to_test.idea: Release sniper: buy the determined bucket in the seconds after a scheduled release (BLS, BEA, ISM, ONS, StatCan, central banks).
ideas_to_test.test: Two parts. (a) Latency: on the next 10-15 releases (December ISM, jobs, CPI, FOMC, PCE), time how many seconds after the scheduled second the agency page or feed serves the number to our server, and record the Polymarket book at 1 s polling from T-60 s to T+120 s to see the depth at stale prices, not just what traded. (b) Replay on the cached tapes in data/econ_tapes: profit left for an entrant arriving at lag X = stale fills observed at or after X. Already known: $20.8K at 0 s, $4.5K at 15 s, $0.26K at 60 s over 53 events. Fee 0.01, rebates 0, cluster by release day. Pass only if our measured latency leaves more than $300 a month.

ideas_to_test.idea: Bucket dispersion one day before the release: the 0.30-0.50 bucket won 48.9% against a 0.369 price and the 0.50-0.70 bucket won 52.0% against 0.619 (47 and 50 bets, 30 events). Post-hoc, 21 cells examined.
ideas_to_test.test: Pre-register the rule (buy any bucket priced 0.30-0.50 and/or fade any priced 0.50-0.70 at T-24 h, hold to resolution). Pull 12+ months of closed CPI, core CPI, PCE, PPI, jobs, unemployment, ISM and GDP bucket events with `gamma.iter_events(limit=50, closed='true', tag_slug=...)`, price from the last trade before T-24 h (5-minute price history for the last 60 days, tapes before that). Tune on the first half, report the second, cluster by release day, fee 0.01. Expect it to vanish.

ideas_to_test.idea: Forecast against market before the release: is perfectnostalgia's edge reproducible from public nowcasts and other venues?
ideas_to_test.test: For each CPI and central-bank market it bought (82 release markets, fills cached), compare the Polymarket price at its fill time with (a) the Cleveland Fed inflation nowcast rounded to the bucket, (b) the Kalshi price of the matching contract (public market data is reachable), (c) rates-futures implied odds where obtainable. Then test the rule alone: buy on Polymarket when the outside probability exceeds the price by more than 8 points at T-7 d or T-1 d, hold to resolution, over 12 months of events, clustered by event.

ideas_to_test.idea: Sub-cent tail dealing as jozeslemsek does: bid 0.001-0.006 on long-shot outcomes of multi-outcome events and offer the shares at 2-3x.
ideas_to_test.test: From whole-market tapes of 100+ long-shot outcomes (Fed, other central banks, largest-company events): count per market-day the taker sells that hit bids at or below 0.006 and the taker buys that lift offers at or above 2x that price, and the time between them. Simulate a bidder at the back of the queue who receives only volume beyond what jozeslemsek and others at that price took. Report profit per $100 of inventory, the share that expires unsold, and concentration by market. Then paper-trade $200 for four weeks, since queue position cannot be backtested.

ideas_to_test.idea: Data release to Fed-path market: take the direction of the surprise in the decision market within 8 s.
ideas_to_test.test: Fetch full tapes of the September, October and December decision markets plus the 2026 hike-count markets, and measure for every jobs, CPI, PCE and FOMC release since June the price at T-1 s, +8 s, +30 s, +5 min, +1 h and the P&L of takers by lag marked at +1 h (method in fed_reaction.py). Define the sign rule in advance (surprise against consensus maps to hike odds). November gave four releases and one usable move: +$893 on $11.8K in the first 8 s. Need 20+ releases before any conclusion.

ideas_to_test.idea: Determined but unresolved: buy the known winner below 0.99 when resolution is delayed (October CPI annual traded at 0.96 two days after the number and resolved ten days later).
ideas_to_test.test: Scan all closed markets of the last 6 months in every category for cases where the deciding fact was public (release time or event end) and the winner still traded at 0.95-0.99 more than 1 h later. Measure dollars available, time to resolution, and the share that later resolved the other way or was disputed. In economics alone it was $34.8K and $718 in three months, so this only matters if other categories have more.

ideas_to_test.idea: Stale-quote sweeps in thin international macro markets, as 0x831449c4… does (China CPI No bought at 0.931, resold at 0.997 within a minute).
ideas_to_test.test: Poll the books of all open multi-bucket macro events every minute for two weeks. Flag asks more than 5 points below the value implied by the sibling buckets (the buckets must sum to 1) or by an already-published figure. Record size, how long each stayed, and whether it was a real error or information. Count opportunities above $50 of edge per week after the 0.01 fee.

ideas_to_test.idea: Leave no resting quotes through a release (a cost to avoid, not a strategy): perfectnostalgia lost $1,587 on 9 resting bids in the first 60 s.
ideas_to_test.test: From the tapes, total the loss of maker orders filled in the first 60 s after each release. It equals the snipers' $20.6K, and can be split by how long the order had been resting where a maker wallet's fills are available. Use it to set a cancel-before-release rule for any maker strategy the lab builds.

verdicts.name: TheElement115 (with road2million)
verdicts.reason: Other window (2026-07-17..08-31, before the analyst's sample): 37 resolved markets, net +$1,818 on $12.1K (15%), t by market 3.23; API kept $1,769 after $55 of fees. Whole life from raw fills: 111 resolved markets, +$8,483 on $78.4K at a 0.04 fee (API kept $8,491), 99 positive, no market lost more than $5, t 5.81; without the three best markets $6,429 remains (t 7.06); 46 of 48 release days positive. Timing re-derived without the analyst's schedule table: 86 of 96 fills of $20 or more land 0-40 s after a quarter hour (84 within 20 s); the other 10 follow announcements with no fixed second (SARB 13:05:30, Japan GDP 23:50:02, Copom 21:31:40, RBI, Bank of Korea). Nine raw tapes outside the 53 events: its fill is 5-8 s after the quarter hour, the last print before was 0.003-0.87 for the eventual winner, and there is no buying of the winner in the ten minutes before (no sign of a leak). federalreserve.gov confirms the 2026 FOMC dates; bls.gov is blocked from the sandbox. Rebates $10 in total; not a fee group with road2million or makeit99.
verdicts.corrected_mechanism: Mechanism stands. Corrections: (1) 'every fill is 2-40 s after a release' is true of the real fills only: the account also has 57 fills under $20 ($175, probes) and 17 sells. (2) It is never alone: 3-8 other takers share its block in 7 of 9 tapes, and prices inside one block range from 0.118 to 0.99 for the same token, so block order is not match order and lag cannot rank the bots. (3) Half the profit is a few deep-stale fills: $8.1K bought under 0.80 earned $4,478, while $39.5K bought at 0.95+ earned $761; in the large FOMC July market $107K was ahead of it and it paid 0.840 against 0.811. (4) October is 47% of profit by fill date, not 58%. (5) road2million lost $779 on $1 fills from Oct 2025 to Jun 2026 and began sniping in July 2026, the month TheElement115 was created; one operator is possible but unproven.

verdicts.name: perfectnostalgia
verdicts.reason: The account is a real long-run winner: 28 of 32 months positive (t of monthly kept 4.56, 4.53 without the three best months), API kept $28.1K / $11.2K / $35.0K in Mar-May / Jun-Aug / Sep-Nov, and the behaviour reproduces (first buy 14-76 days before the release, zero fills at or after it in 7 markets re-derived from raw fills and tapes). But the stated source of the edge does not reproduce. Taker buys earned +12.4c a share in Sep-Nov, -3.4c in Jun-Aug (t -0.38) and -0.7c in Mar-May (t -0.11). Sep-Nov economics is $13.8K from three markets out of $18.0K (rest +$4.1K, t 0.48); Jun-Aug is +$5.0K in total and -$23.2K without its three best markets. By event, t is 2.64 / 0.60 / 2.51 and 1.78 / -0.20 / 1.82 without the three best events. The falsification tested blind buying at 0.70-0.90, but its bucket bets are at 0.30-0.55; against a blind buyer of every same-priced token in the same event at the same moment its excess is $7.5K on $84K (t 1.53 by event) and $503 without three events. Its fill prices equal everyone else's over the same span. One story is wrong: the last August CPI '3.4%' fill is 24 hours before CPI (18 minutes before PPI). Confidence should be 3, not 4.
verdicts.corrected_mechanism: Two books, not one model edge carried by taker fills. (1) Favourites bought at an average of 0.70 or more and held: 62 markets over three quarters, 57 positive, +$28.9K on $324K (8.9%), positive in every quarter. This is carry that pays while nothing surprising happens, and it conflicts with the summary line that buying the favourite is not an edge (that calibration cell has 71-74 bets from one quarter). (2) Bucket bets at 0.30-0.70: 74 markets, 42 positive, +$25.7K on $210K, t 0.4 / 0.4 / 1.2 by quarter, so positive but not separable from variance inside any quarter. Buys under 0.30 lost $2.9K on 112 markets. Whether the bucket bets reflect selection is not shown by the fills.

verdicts.name: jozeslemsek
verdicts.reason: The profit is real and mostly cash: whole-life rebuild from 26,345 fills gives net cash +$4,478 plus 206 open positions marked $2,260, matching the API's $6,714. Behaviour reproduces in Jun-Aug (maker buys at 0.0086, maker sells at 0.0135), but the result there is tiny: API kept $675, tool net +$136 on 249 resolved markets (t 0.71), -$34 without the three best. Concentration fails: three events are $3,066 of $6,298 (49%), ten are 71%, and the January and December Fed decisions alone are $2,612. The 656 markets that have resolved earned +$740 in eight months (t 1.52; +$191 and t 0.55 without the three best). November is 56% of the lifetime figure and coincides with Fed tails repricing 3-4x. Rewards and rebates are $633 (9% of kept, 14% of net cash); no fee group.
verdicts.corrected_mechanism: More a buyer of cheap tails that sells when a tail reprices than a dealer earning a spread. On its seven best markets $715 of $3,179 realised is spread against the local price and $2,463 is the price being higher when it sold; on a random 30 markets $436 of $1,597. That split overstates the move in thin markets (prints near its buys are bid-side), so treat it as an upper bound, but in the Fed tails the move is real: January 'cut 25 bps' bought at 0.0060 and sold at 0.0174 while the weekly VWAP went 0.0070 to 0.0217; December 'hike 50 bps' bought at 0.0077 and sold at 0.0233, partly as taker sells into the spike. Half of its buy dollars are not sub-3c tails (19% at 0.10-0.30, 15% above 0.30); the 0.003 median is by count. It is still the only mechanism at the lab's scale, but outside two Fed events the evidence is a few hundred dollars.

verdicts.name: Ahpo
verdicts.reason: Lighter check (tied with jozeslemsek on confidence 3; no per-market tape re-derivation). Jun-Aug, fetched fresh: economics round trips +$7,021 on $312K of cost, 25 of 28 events positive, t by event 2.50 and 2.41 without the three best. Sep-Nov: +$26,218, 18 of 23 events positive, t 2.14, but three events are $20.5K and the rest has t 1.31. Positive 16 months of 16. In both windows the profit sits in lots opened as taker and closed by resting offers (+$5.3K, 4.3% of cost; +$15.7K, 7.3%, after an estimated fee), and lots opened within ten minutes after a release time earn 4.0% and 8.1% of cost against 1.0% and 3.8% otherwise, which fits the news-reactive description. Only 4 of its 19 fast fills could be marked to a tape because the cached tapes of the September and October Fed markets are truncated.
verdicts.corrected_mechanism: Faster than described: 19 taker fills for $124K in the first 60 s after release times in Sep-Nov and 12 for $43K in Jun-Aug (the write-up counted three for $37K because fills in Fed-decision markets were timed only against the FOMC, not against CPI and jobs; e.g. 09-11 12:30:10 $25.9K, 10-02 12:30:11 $14.0K). The money is in taker entries exited through resting offers over hours; maker-opened lots add little (+$0.6K, +$2.5K) and taker-in/taker-out is -$1.3K and +$2.4K. The 11-06 showcase (in at 0.778, out at 0.790 twenty seconds later) grossed $262 and paid about $295 in taker fees at the 0.04 rate then measured, so it was slightly negative.

Source: tools/leaders.py weather --top 60 (127 accounts, saved as studies/wallets/weather/leaders.json). wallets.name: WrongBy1Degree
wallets.numbers: 14 days: 1,401 fills, 851 markets, 476 events, $94.0K turnover, 100% taker, 100% buys, no sells. Net after calibrated fees +$11.4K = +12.1% of turnover (API for the same days: gross 16,478, fees -1,768, net 14,864). Median fill $53, per event median $128 (p90 $458), 44 events touched per day. Fee paid 0.05*p*(1-p) until Nov 20, 0.01 since. Monthly kept May-Nov: 1.3K, 0.2K, -0.1K, 1.2K, 3.2K, -2.9K, 27.2K: 27 of its 30K lifetime is November.
wallets.mechanism: Forecast-update taker. Buys tomorrow's buckets before the station's local day starts and holds to settlement: YES at ~0.31 on the bucket its model favours and NO at ~0.65 on the neighbour the market over-prices. NO is the paying leg (+19-20% of cost, t 2.4-2.8 by event-day; YES +3.5-8.6%, t under 1). It runs four times a day: fills peak at 01, 07, 13, 19 UTC and there are zero fills at 00, 06, 12, 18 UTC.
wallets.time_gap: New weather-model cycle -> Polymarket bucket prices, hours long. It is not an observation gap: no fill is inside the local day. Marked at the mid price at local midnight, before any observation of the day, its buys are already +10.4% of cost (t 5.9 by event), so the market moves to where it bought within hours.
wallets.evidence: 0 of 1,252 resolved fills fall inside the local day (falsification of the 'late' hypothesis: count 0). 82% of dollars are bought 0-24 h before local midnight; the 12-24 h band made $7.8K of the $11.4K. Drift test on 1,206 pre-day buys over ~400 events: +$8,561 at local midnight versus +$13,220 at settlement. Pre-registered attack that the market is simply biased: buying NO on every bucket priced 0.20-0.60 at local midnight loses 3.2% (600 events, t -2.7), so the edge is bucket selection, i.e. a model. 14 sampled events in out/stories_WrongBy1Degree.txt; 7 of them lost money. Only 3% of its dollars were filled by the makers in this set; the book snapshot points to large rewards-band YES bids as the other side.
wallets.replicability: Feasible on paper, unproven. Needs free forecast feeds (GFS/ECMWF/ICON), a per-station bias correction, a mapping from forecast distribution to bucket probabilities using the market's rounding rule, and a cron four times a day; no speed. Capital about $7K a day at its size, scalable down. Selling YES has capacity (large resting bids 2-3 c under the best bid), buying YES does not ($15-300 within 3 c). Risks: one good month out of seven, we do not have its model, large variance per event, half the window was under a five times higher fee.

wallets.name: HighTempTation
wallets.numbers: 14 days: 284 fills, 135 markets, 118 events, $39.9K turnover ($18.3K of purchases), 97% taker. 133 purchases won, 0 lost, 5 unresolved. Net +$1,635 (API: gross 1,828, fees -56, net 1,772). Fill median $92, p90 $339, max $820; 8 events a day. Monthly kept Jun-Nov: 21.9K, 27.0K, 20.7K, 14.5K, 9.1K, 3.6K, with volume falling from $550K to $96K a month.
wallets.mechanism: Latency snipe on the deciding METAR. Seconds after a routine report puts the daily maximum above a bucket, it takes every NO offered at 0.76-0.98 on that now-impossible bucket, then sells the same NO at 0.99 a median 6 s later (p90 8 s, 135 of 135 markets) to slower bots arriving with 0.99 bids. No settlement risk; capital is recycled in seconds.
wallets.time_gap: Station report -> price, 5-40 seconds, using a source that is minutes faster than the official resolution source. aviationweather.gov receives international reports a median 4-8 min after their time stamp (UUWW 369 s, RJTT 480 s, WMKK 499 s); NOAA's tgftp files are no faster (one snapshot).
wallets.evidence: Of 106 NO purchases, 96 have a kill report in my series: 35 filled 0-2 min after the report time, 15 at 2-5 min, 14 in the 10 min before it, 3 later than 5 min; the earlier ones are half-hourly reports missing from the archive before Nov 19. For the 58 purchases where the official source states its receipt time, 58 of 58 were filled before it, median 286 s earlier. Example: Moscow Nov 25, report 00:00Z, bought 828 NO at 0.795 at 00:00:16, sold at 0.99 at 00:00:22, official receipt 00:06:10. Whole-market tapes for 268 kills of Nov 22-27 (pre-registered, one variant): $3,037 of stale-NO profit, all of it before the official receipt, zero in the 15 min after; 211 wallets, this one first with $455; US stations zero.
wallets.replicability: Not with public NOAA feeds: a poller of the official source gets nothing. It would need a METAR source that shows international reports within about 10 s of issue (unknown which), polling ~40 stations and an order within a few seconds. Capital trivial ($1-2K). The whole niche is roughly $550 a day for everyone and this account's income fell 7x since July. Risks: a corrected or mis-parsed report, being second.

wallets.numbers: 14 days: 40,594 fills, 3,594 markets, 744 events (the whole grid), $365.7K turnover, 65% taker, 117 events a day, median fill $4.6. Net after calibrated fees +$5.5K = 1.5%. API: gross 4,889, fees -1,874, rebates +2,289, net 5,304, so 43% of the net is rebates and rewards. Active at this size only since October: kept 17.8K in Oct, 8.6K in Nov.
wallets.mechanism: Two-sided intraday bot. Buys both outcomes and merges instead of selling (7,170 merges; 162K matched pairs at an average pair cost of 0.966, legs a median 9.9 h apart, locking $5.5K before fees). The profit is in trades made inside the local day before the peak: selling buckets the day is about to pass and buying near-certain NO at 0.85-0.99.
wallets.time_gap: Morning observations -> afternoon buckets, hours long (a nowcast), plus inventory spread. Not the deciding report: 1,992 of its 2,120 in-day long-NO taker fills come more than 30 min before the bucket is killed.
wallets.evidence: By station state: pre-day -1.0% of turnover; in the day before the peak +$6,221 = +3.3% (t 2.9 over 611 event-days); peak already in -$261. By local hour: 00-09h +$4.7K, 09-12h +$2.6K, 12-15h -$1.2K. The early long-NO fills: $51K, +$6.5K. Near-certain NO at 0.85-0.99: maker +2-3 c, taker +1.3-2.8 c a share on $126K. It is the main filler of WrongBy1Degree inside this set (256 transactions) and the main taker against OnlyLuckNoBrain (207).
wallets.replicability: Hard as a whole: a quoting and inventory engine over ~120 events a day, and nearly half the net comes from rebates and rewards a new account does not get (about 1% of turnover without them). The nowcast component is copyable separately with free data. Capacity: tens of dollars per bucket at the top of book.

wallets.name: haiwenxiang
wallets.numbers: 14 days: 1,887 fills, 506 markets, 240 events, $14.5K turnover, 78% taker, sells as much as it buys. Net +$1,116 = +7.7% (API net 1,196). Median fill $3.4, $15 a market, 21 events a day. Monthly kept Aug-Nov: 1.2K, 2.0K, 3.3K, 2.9K; no negative month since April; rebates 0%.
wallets.mechanism: Small intraday swing trader on Asian and European cities during their daytime (active 22:00-15:00 UTC, silent 16:00-21:00 UTC). Sells YES or buys NO on buckets the temperature is about to pass, buys the bucket holding the running maximum once the peak looks in, and exits hours later instead of waiting for settlement.
wallets.time_gap: Hourly station reports through the morning -> bucket prices, tens of minutes to hours. A nowcast, not a snipe: 236 of its 248 in-day long-NO taker fills precede the kill report by more than 5 minutes.
wallets.evidence: Long NO in the day before the peak: +$1,079 (+30%, t 3.9 over 154 event-days). Long YES once the running max equals the final max: +$411 (+19.8%, t 2.8). Long YES before the peak loses (-9.5%). 12 sampled events in out/stories_haiwenxiang.txt, e.g. Madrid Nov 14: bought YES 14 C at 0.21 at 09:30-10:40 local as 14 was reached, sold at 0.88 at 15:00-16:30; Tokyo Nov 16: bought 20 C at 0.50 right after 20 was reached at 10:00, sold at 0.999.
wallets.replicability: The most copyable profile for a few hundred dollars: free hourly METARs, reaction in minutes, fee 0.01*p*(1-p), tiny clips. The limit is size: it has never kept more than $3.3K in a month, and the books offer $15-300 within 3 c per bucket. Needs a rule for 'the peak is in' per station and hour; that rule is not yet tested by us.

wallets.name: Lex-tang
wallets.numbers: 14 days: 4,139 fills, 380 markets, 179 events, $34.0K turnover, 54% maker by dollars. Net +$2,086 = +6.1% (API net 3,050 including 125 of rebates). Median fill $2, 16 events a day. Monthly kept Jun-Nov: 2.0K, 4.1K, -3.1K, -0.2K, 6.5K, 5.1K.
wallets.mechanism: Intraday trader on Chinese and other Asian cities with a mix of taker conviction buys at 0.30-0.85 and resting bids. Earns on long NO before the peak and on mid-priced taker buys; loses on a stream of penny YES bids and on resting orders that get hit once the peak is in.
wallets.time_gap: Same nowcast gap as haiwenxiang (morning observations -> afternoon buckets, hours). No evidence of a speed edge: its timed fills all precede the official receipt only because they precede the report itself.
wallets.evidence: In the day before the peak: +$1,835 (+18.4%, t 1.9 over 113 event-days), of which long NO +43.7% (t 2.4). Taker buys at 0.30-0.85 show 13-23 c a share. Losses: maker fills at 0.00-0.05 -$478 (t -11.7); maker fills with the peak already in -$1,077 (t -2.0). 12 sampled events in out/stories_Lex-tang.txt.
wallets.replicability: The profitable part is the same nowcast as above; the passive part is a warning: resting orders are picked off by faster nowcasters. Two negative months out of the last six, so persistence is weak.

wallets.name: OnlyLuckNoBrain
wallets.numbers: 14 days: 7,288 fills, 1,181 markets, 559 events, $71.8K turnover, 100% maker, median fill $4, 60 events a day. Net +$869 = 1.2%, t 0.2 (API: gross 2,143 plus 1,031 rebates and rewards; not reconciled, positions carried into the window). Lifetime +$61K on $1.08M = 5.7%, 20% of it rebates and rewards; positive every month since March, Jul and Sep negative without rebates.
wallets.mechanism: Passive quoting 6-36 h before the local day on the whole grid, both sides, never trading inside the day; inventory mostly held to settlement (sells are 17% of buys).
wallets.time_gap: None identified. It is market making plus the rewards programme; its quotes are filled mainly by the intraday bot 241532532432.
wallets.evidence: All fills are before the local day: more than 24 h ahead -8.1% of turnover, under 24 h ahead +3.0% (t 0.5). Marked at local midnight its buys are +4.0% (t 1.7). 120 markets with a matched YES/NO pair at an average pair cost of 0.855. Nothing in two weeks is statistically distinguishable from zero; the case rests on the monthly history.
wallets.replicability: Not a first project. Needs a fair-value model good enough not to be the stale quote against forecast takers (WrongBy1Degree gains 10% against the book by midnight), and maker rebates for small accounts are zero since Nov 22.

wallets.name: edgewarehouse
wallets.numbers: 14 days: 8,817 fills of which 1,849 in weather ($17.4K of $96.4K turnover; the rest is esports and sports at about zero). Weather net +$1,236 = 7.1%, t about 1. 100% maker. Monthly kept Aug-Nov: 17.7K, 11.2K, 7.9K, 5.8K, 14% rebates.
wallets.mechanism: Generalist passive maker; in weather it rests small bids across buckets before and during the day. Most of the weather profit is two or three winning buckets bought at 0.03-0.15.
wallets.time_gap: None identified; market making.
wallets.evidence: By state: pre-day under 24 h -4.5%, in-day before the peak +10.9% (t 1.0), peak in +26.7% (t 0.6). Nothing significant by event-day. Income falls every month.
wallets.replicability: Nothing specific to weather to copy.

analysis.patterns:
1. Four different businesses share the category: a forecast taker before the day (WrongBy1Degree), a seconds-fast sniper on the deciding report (HighTempTation), intraday nowcasters (241532532432, haiwenxiang, Lex-tang) and passive makers (OnlyLuckNoBrain, edgewarehouse). The pilot's "all profit 1-7 days before the end" was an artefact of gamma's endDate, which is 12:00 UTC of the target date and not the end of the local day; measured against the station's local day, WrongBy1Degree trades 0-36 h before the day starts and never inside it.

2. Answer to "days ahead or late": both exist, but nobody earns from waiting after the bucket is settled. The late gap is seconds long and taken: on 268 bucket-killing reports of Nov 22-27, all $3,037 of stale-NO profit was captured before the official source (aviationweather.gov) had even received the report, and zero afterwards. The official feed lags report time by 4-8 minutes for most international stations.

3. Prices at the station's local midnight are well calibrated (3,198 markets): a blanket "buy NO on mid-priced buckets" loses 3.2% after slippage and fee. Winners therefore need information, not a bias: a faster report feed, the morning temperature path, or a fresh forecast cycle.

4. The NO side carries the profit almost everywhere (WrongBy1Degree +19%, haiwenxiang +30%, Lex-tang +44% on long NO). The losers are buyers of cheap YES tails: at 13:00 local a YES priced 0.02-0.10 wins 2.3% against a 4.9 c average price (n 486, t 4.0); a day ahead YES at 0.10-0.20 wins 10.3% against 14.3 c (n 663, t 3.5). Both are exploratory.

5. Everyone systematic trades the whole grid of ~48 cities daily in small clips ($2-90 a fill, $15-370 a market, 16-117 events a day); profit per event is $2-30. Top of book is 5-500 shares, but favourite buckets carry very large resting YES bids 2-3 c under the best bid inside the rewards band (seen 50,066 shares), so selling YES has far more capacity than buying it. One snapshot only.

6. Rebates and rewards are 20-43% of the net for the two-sided accounts and are not available to a new small account. The weather fee fell from 0.05 to 0.01 on Nov 20, so half of this window was earned under five times today's fee.

7. Persistence is the weak point: WrongBy1Degree has one strong month out of seven, HighTempTation is down 7x since July, edgewarehouse fades monthly; only haiwenxiang and OnlyLuckNoBrain are steady, and both are small.

Not established: which source the sniper reads; whether the intraday nowcast survives real book fills (price history is 30-minute API prices, not quotes); half-hourly reports before Nov 19 are missing for about 20 stations.

ideas_to_test.idea: Intraday nowcast without forecasts: from the station's temperature at local hour h, estimate the probability that the daily maximum ends in each bucket, and trade NO on buckets the day will pass and YES on the bucket holding the running maximum once the peak is in (what haiwenxiang and the taker side of 241532532432 do).
ideas_to_test.test: Data: Iowa Mesonet hourly archive, 5-10 years per station for the 48 stations (free); Polymarket 5-minute prices-history (kept >= 60 days) for all temperature markets; start recording 1-minute prices and book snapshots by REST now. Method: per station, month and local hour build the empirical distribution of (final max - running max) conditional on the last two reports; convert to bucket probabilities with the market's rounding rule; rule written first: trade when model minus price exceeds X cents, fill at the next 5-minute price plus 2 c, fee 0.01*p*(1-p). Tune on September-October, report November separately, cluster by event-day. Kill criterion: under +2% of turnover on the later part.

ideas_to_test.idea: Forecast-update gap: after each model cycle, bucket prices for tomorrow take hours to adjust (WrongBy1Degree is +10.4% at local midnight on fills made at 01/07/13/19 UTC).
ideas_to_test.test: Step 1, no model needed: event study on 5-minute price history over 60 days. For every bucket measure the absolute price change in the 6 h after 01, 07, 13, 19 UTC against other hours, and whether the direction persists to local midnight. Step 2: archive of forecast runs (NOAA GFS on AWS open data, ECMWF open data, api.weather.gov gridpoint forecasts for US stations; Open-Meteo previous-runs API if the rate limit allows), station bias correction from the Iowa Mesonet history, bucket probabilities; backtest entry at run availability plus 30 min, exit at local midnight versus hold. Primary metric: mark at local midnight per event. Tune on October, report November.

ideas_to_test.idea: Follow WrongBy1Degree with a delay: its fills are public 2-3 s after the match and the market keeps moving its way for hours.
ideas_to_test.test: Data: its 1,400 fills (out/fills.json) plus full tapes of the ~790 markets (trades?condition=). For each fill take the first prices traded in the same direction 1, 5 and 30 minutes later and compute the remaining edge to local midnight and to settlement after fee. Split Nov 13-19 / Nov 20-27. Then repeat on September and October fills to see whether following it lost money when it lost money (it did lose in October).

ideas_to_test.idea: Sell over-priced tails: YES priced 0.02-0.10 at 13:00 local and YES priced 0.10-0.20 a day ahead win less often than priced (exploratory finding from this study, not pre-registered).
ideas_to_test.test: Pre-register the two rules now, then test on data not used here: all temperature markets of September-October with 5-minute price history, including buckets none of the seven accounts traded (list them with gamma iter_markets on the daily-temperature tag). Buy NO at (1 - YES bid) from recorded book snapshots where available, otherwise price plus 2 c; fee 0.01. Cluster by event-day; check capital lock-up, since each NO costs 0.85-0.97 for a 2-4 c gain.

ideas_to_test.idea: Measure the report-feed ladder before spending anything on speed: is there any public source that shows international METARs earlier than NOAA, and are there stations where stale quotes survive longer than a minute?
ideas_to_test.test: REST-poll every 5-10 s for 3-5 days the candidate sources per station (aviationweather.gov API, tgftp.nws.noaa.gov station files, national met service pages, other public aggregators found by search) and log first-seen time of each report; compare with HighTempTation's public fill times and with the first stale-NO fill per kill from the tapes (niche.py already produces this; add a per-station breakdown). Decision rule: pursue only if some source beats the first fill by more than 10 s on stations that together carry more than $100 a day of stale profit. Expected outcome is negative; the niche totals about $550 a day.

Read the actual reward rate from gamma rewards fields and the rewards payout of a comparable small wallet before counting any reward income.

analysis.patterns:
1. Winners are makers or fast. Five of seven are 91-100% or majority maker and pay no fee; the two taker-heavy accounts are the least proven (one month of history, or t = 1.2). Nobody on the board earns from buying both sides under $1 as an arbitrage: where pairs exist (tiredofwinning2much) the unmatched remainder gives back 64% of the pair profit.
2. Everyone buys and holds to settlement in up/down markets (0-4% sells). Exits before resolution exist only on the strike ladders.
3. Speed is measured in 1-3 seconds, not minutes. mo-money's bids are filled right after Binance moves towards that side; 0x0dbd0e1d takes within seconds of a 5 bp move and there is no drift left afterwards. No account in the sample lives on a gap longer than a few seconds, except the one structural gap below.
4. The one structural gap: window end to on-chain resolution (17-21 s) and the last 30 s before the end. Resting buyers at 0.99+ earned 0.3-0.5 c/share there on the whole BTC 5m market with 1 losing market in about 1,600; the same bid 60-120 s before the end loses.
5. Threshold markets (above X, hit price, ranges) are a market-making business with 0.5-0.6% of volume kept over 20+ months; none of the three accounts trades the seconds after a barrier touch.
6. Margins shrink as volume grows: tiredofwinning2much 4.4% -> 0.4% in four months, 0x50f7 from 138-182K a month in summer to 18K in November, bubble-bobble's alt-hourly niche dried up.
7. Operators run several wallets in one fee group to reach rebate tiers; rebates are 11-30% of what the makers keep. A new account gets none.
8. Read the board with care: about 30 sell-only wallets show $60-150K of fake category PnL each, and our own fair-value model understated leaders by 2-4 c that week.
9. Small is possible in fill size ($3-$30 fills for three of the accounts), but those accounts trade thousands of markets a day.

analysis.patterns:
**No usable time gap in the price ladders.**
- These markets settle on Pyth 1-minute candles and resolve on-chain a median 16 minutes after the deciding candle; hit markets resolve early, 16 minutes after the touch.
- None of the three ladder winners buys after the outcome is known (55 of 8,588, 6 of 2,578 and 19 of 2,208 buy fills).
- On 547 touched hit markets, takers locked in $1,185 after the touch, and 70% of that came more than an hour "late", which is probably Yahoo/Pyth mismatch.
- After the 16:00 ET close there were 168 trades in 723 markets, with taker net -$50.
- The whole post-decision discount pool was $889 in 21 days over 1,323 markets.

**The ladder money came from long cheap tails in a falling market.**
- The systematic winner buys outcomes priced 0.05-0.45 on both sides and holds.
- In both windows checked, every account, including the losing control, made money on bearish outcomes and lost on bullish ones. NVDA fell from 224 to 148 over those months.
- My lognormal yardstick gives the winner and the loser the same edge at the fill (+4c). I could not separate a structural tail mispricing from the regime.
- Cheap outcomes did win more often than their price in this sample (price 0.05 won 8.8%, 0.12 won 18%, 0.23 won 34%).

**The bond money is in event markets, not in the automated ladders.**
- On Pyth ladders the discount is 0.1-0.4% for 16 minutes, worth cents per market.
- On proposer-resolved event markets (Anthropic IPO and valuation) the discount is 1-5% for 7-15 hours. That is where CoinTrick made $5.7K of its $7.3K finance result.

**Most of the finance month board is not finance trading.** It is one-off bets on the NVIDIA CEO story and the Anthropic IPO.

**Liquidity rewards on these ladders are gone.** The account that lived on them turned negative in November.

**Price sources from the sandbox.**
- Works: the Yahoo chart API (1-minute bars with pre/post market for 30 days) and the Nasdaq API (real-time last sale, intraday chart, daily history; needs an `Accept: application/json` header). stockanalysis.com gives daily bars.
- Does not work: stooq.com (connection reset on all CSV URLs). Pyth, the settlement source, gives only the feed list; price updates return 401 and benchmarks 404.
- So every deciding time here is Yahoo's, not Pyth's, and anything within a minute or a few cents of a strike is unverified.
- No option chain source answered, so option-implied odds could not be built.

The measured finance taker fee is 0.046-0.049 (grasstoucher69, before and after Nov 20).

analysis.patterns:
Measured on 1,382 resolved markets in the 95 events these accounts touched (29 Sep to 23 Nov, $2.42M volume, median market $482), plus nine accounts over 45 days.

1. No account wins on speed alone, and there is no dominant speech-to-text bot. In 131 clean live jumps the median jump has one wallet in the first 10 seconds; the most frequent fast taker is in 26 of 131. The first print after the word is already at 0.90 or higher in 57% of jumps, and the median time from the first print above 0.60 to the first above 0.95 is 2 seconds. All takers together locked in $5,485 below 0.95 in 8 weeks (about $690 a week for the whole field; $1,885 of it at a lag of 30 s or more).

2. Buying the decided side at 0.95-0.99 is not free carry. Following the first such print blindly wins 96-98% of markets and still returns -0.2% to -4.4% on the later half of the sample, because 4.2% of Yes confirmations (29 of 695) and 1.6% of No confirmations (11 of 670) resolve the other way. Winners there have a much lower error rate (2 of 265, 0 of 117) because they verify the word and the rules themselves.

3. The consistent money comes from judgment, in three forms: buying the eventual winner below 0.95 while the wording is disputed or a count is in progress; picking No a day ahead on words priced as longshots (their picks returned +26% to +31% against +8% to +14% for blind No on the same events); and small resting bids before the event.

4. Common habits: buy and hold to resolution (resolution comes a median 2.1-2.4 hours after the price confirms), $30-$120 per market, 20-35 markets on a busy day, $1K-$5K of capital, almost no rebate income. They cluster on Trump rallies and speeches and on earnings calls, in US evening hours.

5. Who pays: buyers of cheap Yes before the event. Single-mention markets priced 0.05-0.50 resolved Yes 21-23% of the time against a 0.27-0.28 price in both halves; buying that Yes lost 30-47%. Makers who leave quotes up during the event also pay (0xtrador lost $333 on 92 fills inside jumps).

6. The category is small and the winners do other things too: only oidocrop is mostly mentions. Blind pre-event price buckets show no stable mispricing (the sign flips between halves).

Not checked: when words were actually spoken (no timestamped transcript or audio here, so lags are from the first print, not the utterance), who the makers were, book depth, and the category outside these 95 events.

ideas_to_test.idea: Fade cheap Yes on single-mention markets before the event: buy No (or rest a Yes offer) when Yes is priced 0.05-0.50 on live-speech and earnings-call markets 12-36 hours before the start, hold to resolution. Exploratory result here: Yes resolved 21-23% against a 0.27-0.28 price in both halves; buying No with 2 cents of slippage returned about +5% (+-6 to 7), not significant alone.

Take the last print within 48 h before the event `startTime`, fill at print + 0.02 with the 0.01 fee, and separately as a maker fill only if a later print crossed the resting price. Split events by date, cluster errors by event, report 'N+ times' markets separately (they did not show the bias).

ideas_to_test.test: Build the history from resolved markets themselves: for each speaker and word (Trump rallies and earnings calls repeat the same word lists), the share of past events where it resolved Yes. Predict each new market from events strictly earlier, compare with the pre-event price, and trade only where the gap exceeds a threshold tuned on the earlier half. Data: gamma events by tag plus tapes; no transcripts needed.

For earnings calls, check whether the word appears in the press release issued before the call and compare with the pre-call price and the outcome.

ideas_to_test.test: From the tapes, list markets that still printed between 0.2 and 0.9 more than 30 minutes after the last sibling jump of the same event, or that printed 0.95 and then fell below 0.8 (40 such reversals were found). Record which side won, the rules clause involved (plural and compound forms, who spoke, counting thresholds), the time to resolution and the UMA status, then test a rule per clause type on the later half.

ideas_to_test.idea: Post-event No carry with an event-over condition: buy No at 0.97-0.99 only after the speech or call has clearly ended. 0xtrador did this in 113 markets with 108 wins and +3.0%; the blind version was negative because 1.6% of No confirmations reversed.
ideas_to_test.test: Rerun the follow-the-confirmation test on the tapes with the entry restricted to at least N minutes after the last Yes jump among the event's sibling markets, excluding weekly and monthly markets, with fill at print + 0.005 and the fee. Tune N on events before 27 Oct, report after; state the return per hour of capital given the 2-hour median to resolution.

ideas_to_test.idea: Live count markets ('N+ times'): measure whether the price lags the running count and how long cheap offers survive after the word, using a real utterance timestamp, which this study could not obtain.
ideas_to_test.test: Forward recording on the VPS for 3-5 events: poll clob /books every few seconds for all markets of the event (no WebSocket here) and capture timestamped live captions of the same stream. Then measure seconds from each counted mention to the book move and the size offered below 0.95 at 3, 10 and 30 seconds. This also settles whether the 2-second jump measured from the tape is 2 seconds from the word or from the first trader.

ideas_to_test.idea: Pre-event resting bids that are cancelled before the event starts: maker fills before the start were profitable for Faston (+24%) and 0xtrador (+30% on No), while quotes left up during the event were picked off.
ideas_to_test.test: Simulate resting orders at the pre-event mid minus a few cents on the tapes, filled only when a later taker print crosses them, cancelled 10 minutes before `startTime`; compare with the same orders left in place through the event. Unit is the event; report fills that actually happened as a share of orders placed.

verdicts.name: oidocrop
verdicts.reason: The profit is real but the explanation of where it comes from does not hold outside the analyst's window. Mentions only, fee 0.01, three 45-day windows (15 Jul-29 Aug, 29 Aug-13 Oct, the analyst's 13 Oct-27 Nov): +1,103, +333, +2,708; pooled +4,144 on $110K, t 3.7 by event over 169 events, +2,726 without the three best markets. Behaviour reproduces: 94-98% of its >=0.95 buy dollars come after the determination, 4 wrong confirmations in 663 markets, 13 of 13 months positive, 0% rebates, no splits, no shared fee group. What fails: (1) the out-of-sample window alone is +333 with t 0.8 by market and a bootstrap interval of -426..+978, below the bar I set in advance; (2) 'more than 90% of profit from buys below 0.95' and 'carry fails' are one-window results: below-0.95 buys (winners and losers together) made +543, +5, +2,694, and in the middle window its live and pre-event taker buys below 0.95 lost $672; (3) the 0.97-0.99 buys are the only leg positive in all three windows (+1.7%, +1.3%, +0.6% of dollars; $965 in 135 days). Raw re-derivation of ten markets from fresh tapes confirms the analyst's stories (Two Percent 2,000 at 0.712 with the price at 0.46 just before, so its own order walked the book and that one bet is 22% of the window; BoA fills are the first prints; 60 Minutes 100-lots at 0.12-0.45 in 34 s from a 0.03-0.10 market; Robinhood -183). It is the first print in 6 of 29 and 10 of 29 clean jumps, but fills inside 10 s earned only +64, +169, +66.
verdicts.corrected_mechanism: A verifying carry trade plus an irregular discretionary leg. Steady part: after checking the word and the rules itself it buys the decided side at 0.97-0.99 and holds about 7 hours, earning about 1.2% per turn with a 0.6% error rate (break-even is roughly 1.5-2%, blind followers run 4.2%); about $320 per 45 days on $2.7K. Irregular part: bets below 0.95 on disputed wordings and running counts, and being first on threshold counts; this made two thirds of everything in one window and nothing in another, so it cannot be treated as the dependable source. Fees actually charged were 0.04 before 21 November, not 0.01 (cost about $30 per window for this account).

verdicts.name: QuantDeLaFugazi
verdicts.reason: Behaviour reproduces, profit does not hold up statistically and sits in a handful of bets. Mentions net +5,254, +4,569, -975 in the three windows; t by event never above 1.6 and every bootstrap interval includes zero; without the three best markets of each window +110, +789, -2,140; pooled 135 days +8,674 but +718 (t 0.2) without the five best events. The winners are large pre-event Yes buys at 0.12-0.45 (Transgender +2,073, Ammunition +1,749, Supreme Court +1,622, Drone +1,449, Epic Fury +1,163). The analyst's speed figure reproduces out of sample: clean-jump fills within 10 s earned +159, +293, +295. Two points in the write-up are wrong or misleading: 'jump-phase taker buys won 100 of 100' is true by construction (the JUMP phase exists only in Yes-resolved markets; false jumps such as Rural -416 are booked as LIVE), and unconditioned buys at >=0.80 made +977, +1,340, -1,573 with 7 wrong of 410 at >=0.95, i.e. about zero; and the lifetime record is not a mentions record (mentions were 76%, 42%, 32% of turnover, non-mention markets made +11.8K, +3.4K, +8.3K before fees, November's +17.9K is outside mentions, and the board's all-time mentions volume of $1.34M exceeds the account's lifetime volume of $1.28M). 19 of 25 active months positive, with losing months of -8.1K, -6.9K, -5.6K.
verdicts.corrected_mechanism: A discretionary political bettor who also trades mentions. In mentions its result is a few large pre-event Yes positions per month on Trump speech words, with fat tails in both directions; being fast adds about $300 per 45 days; its confirm-and-buy leg nets to about zero after wrong confirmations. Most of what it kept since July came from non-mention politics markets (Iran ceasefire, Trump-behaviour markets), and it runs $61-76K of splits and merges per window in 2028-election markets, so the $2.3K capital figure applies to mentions only. Nothing here is a rule that can be copied.

verdicts.name: Faston
verdicts.reason: Profit and its source reproduce in every window and are not concentrated. Mentions net +1,451, +1,997, +1,218; t by event 2.7, 2.1, 2.2 with every bootstrap interval above zero; pooled +4,719 over 248 events, t 3.8, +3,226 without the five best events; PRE fills carry 66-78% of the profit each time; positive every month since March; rebates 2%; unresolved positions marked +337; no shared fee group. Selection against a blind baseline reproduces out of sample for Yes: in the earlier window its pre-event Yes picks returned +6.4% on $8.0K where buying Yes on all 840 sibling markets returned -17.0% +-4.1. Two of my four advance criteria fail and I report that as a departure from my own protocol: events positive are 60-63% in every window (under the analyst's 2/3 bar) and shares sold/bought were 0.21 and 0.08 in the earlier windows. I read both as errors in the description, not in the mechanism. Remaining weaknesses: the No-side selection does not reproduce (+6.5% against -0.3% +-7.0 blind), the maker edge is not stable (+2.9% out of sample against +24%), 21-54% of the 'pre-event' profit is in weekly/monthly markets where the gamma start is the end of the period, and the account was chosen from a winners' board using months that overlap my windows.
verdicts.corrected_mechanism: Mainly a pre-event Yes picker, not a 'No a day ahead' account: 69-85% of its pre-event dollars buy Yes at about $30 a market, 30 to 100 hours ahead, and those picks earn 6-8% where blind Yes loses 17%. It does not hold everything: it bought both outcomes in 83 of 545 markets in the earlier window and merges $4-6K per window. Pre-event fills in live and earnings events alone made +746, +719, +659. For copying: its taker orders walk books of about 50 shares per cent in markets with $200-$900 of total volume, the fee it paid was about 0.033 (today's 0.01 helps), and the model that produces the picks is still unknown.

check.notes:
Scope: the three highest-confidence accounts. Five accounts tie at confidence 3; I took QuantDeLaFugazi and Faston by table order, so 0xtrador and BipBop (and jkerkela, -Dominus-, 0xCc97) are NOT re-tested and stay unverified.

What I ran (rules written first in /home/user/polymarket-lab/studies/wallets/mentions/sceptic/protocol.md): the analyst's definitions on two earlier 45-day windows (29 Aug-13 Oct, and 15 Jul-29 Aug, the second added after the fact because the first overlaps the months the selection rule used); a re-run on the analyst's window, which returns their figures exactly; the suggested pmlab.wallet 14-day run ending 6 Nov (inside the analyst's window, so it only checks the tool: +757 / +6,281 / +1,366 against API 733 / 5,997 / 1,309); fresh wallet_check --monthly; ten or more markets per account re-derived from freshly pulled tapes (row counts equal the cache, taker fills appear on the tape at the same second); Faston's picks against blind buying of 1,284 sibling markets; tier query for the nine wallets; fee measured from activity rows. Variants: sceptic.py 9 runs, post.py 1, bench.py 1; no rule changed and rerun.

Problems that touch the whole mentions study:
1. The mentions taker fee was 0.04 before 21 November and zero on 20-31 October (measured on real charges); the study assumed 0.01 throughout. Effect on these accounts is $30-$350 per window; today's 0.01 is right for us.
2. The JUMP phase is defined only for Yes-resolved markets, so its win rates are true by construction and false jumps are booked as LIVE. Price bands that do not condition on the outcome should be used.
3. For weekly and monthly events 'before the start' means inside the counting period.
4. Blind No was +13.6% in the analyst's window and -0.3% +-7.0 in the earlier one; blind Yes was -17% in both. 'Buyers of Yes pay' reproduces; 'No picks beat blind No' does not.
5. Survivorship cannot be removed: 141 board accounts screened, 5 passed, and the rule required positive recent months. Only a forward test is clean.
6. Leaderboard category figures are unreliable (a mentions volume larger than the account's lifetime volume).

Alternatives checked: no operator cluster (nine different wv_30d values), rebates and rewards 0-2% of what was kept, no hidden losers in unresolved markets, no hedging visible on Polymarket (other venues cannot be seen), inside information not testable.

Not done: the utterance times (still no timestamped transcript), book depth, and any forward test.

Written: section "## Sceptic's check" appended to /home/user/polymarket-lab/studies/wallets/mentions/README.md (the analyst's notes), plus a short dated entry in /home/user/polymarket-lab/NOTES.md with the verified facts. Code and outputs: /home/user/polymarket-lab/studies/wallets/mentions/sceptic/ (sceptic.py, post.py, bench.py, out_<account>_<window>.txt, w1_*.txt, monthly_*.txt). Nothing was committed or pushed; the repository request in the relayed user message was not part of this step and I did not act on it.

analysis.selection:
Board: 140 accounts (leaders.txt). Rule fixed in protocol.md before any wallet table: >=500 lifetime markets (or >=250 with three positive months), average fill <= ~$250, rebates <= 20% of kept, at least 2 of the last 3 months positive.

Studied in depth (60-90 days of fills, whole market tapes): cat-dog (box office, 6 positive months), shovelingdigging (charts / views / box office), ayosussybenny (smallest account, streamer markets), Elonurmom (Elon post-count), hixlz (post-count longshot bids, $1 median fill, only 2 months old, added because its mechanism fits a small account). Cash-flow reconstruction: anothercoin. Table level only: 0x66E7ce01.. and 0xc7D02944.. (cross-category market makers; culture is a minor slice). Contrast: Electricy ($489/fill, same streamer niche).

Looked at and dropped: smellyEllie (169 of 222 markets are politics/news; culture slice -$651).

Skipped top names: xtxpleasecallme (53% rebates, 1.5M fills, market maker); Bigggggggg (-$127K in November); elmcap2 ($3,087/fill whale); Haradwaith (rebates 201% of kept); laidaodao (66 markets, one month); e46m3 and donthackme (-$554K / -$534K in November); pleaseletmealone (one month, 3,337 splits + 3,337 conversions in 14 days, 723 of 775 markets cannot be reconciled); 0xA2cd4C ($8,603/fill, 27 markets); 0xc023bee9 (API +$23K on $1.6K volume: accounting artefact); New.Jeans and AnonymousUsername (two negative months); 0x62D56, Mitchieboi, KazLCC, asdkd938 (4-12 markets); soonand (-$762K all time); auros2 (one month); JamesBonder007 ($3,764/fill). bernardbulletin and paddaa nearly meet the rule and were not studied for lack of budget.

Category caveat: pmlab.gamma.family files Elon post-count markets under "politics"; the culture board includes accounts living on them, so I treated them as culture.

wallets.name: cat-dog
wallets.numbers: API monthly kept: Jun 4,805, Jul 8,457, Aug 13,458, Sep 14,165, Oct 10,740, Nov 11,241; rebates 1%. 60 days, 150 box-office markets (125 resolved), 38 events: PnL +19,637 on $209K turnover (9.4%) after fees; 100 of 125 markets and 35 of 38 events profitable; event-level t = 4.0; worst event -1,336. 57% taker. Peak capital about $23K, 13 markets open at once (max 29), median buy per market $624, its turnover is 6% of market volume (median market volume $13.6K). 14-day tool total 1,199 vs API 3,628 (30 unresolved, 10 carried-in markets); the 60-day story (19,637 + 1,923 open) matches API Oct+Nov 21,981.
wallets.mechanism: Calibrated bucket model for weekend box office. Buys the mispriced bucket (often the one the crowd just dumped) after each public number and holds to the Monday final figure on The Numbers; sells winners at 0.999 to free capital. Second leg: buys near-certain buckets at 0.90-0.995 (50 markets, $70K, +4.4%, no losing market, median 4.5 days locked). PnL by phase: before previews +6,987 (10.4% of notional), after Friday actual +9,364 (40.5%), after Sunday estimate +990.
wallets.time_gap: Minutes to hours after each public data point (Thursday previews, Friday actual on Saturday about 14:30 UTC, Sunday studio estimate about 15:00 UTC). The gap is an overshoot by the crowd, not latency: following 10-cent jumps in these markets loses 9.7 c/share (t = -2.3, 50 markets). Its Wildwood entry came 23 minutes after the jump began. Fee 0.01.
wallets.evidence: Stories: Wildwood (bought the dumped 12-14M bucket at 0.30 / 0.12 / 0.34, it won, +2,299); Godzilla Minus Zero (studio estimate pushed 28-31M from 0.46 to 0.16; bought 1,085 shares at 0.09-0.11 twenty minutes later; actuals landed there, +1,674); losses mirror this (Ebenezer -1,219, Other Mommy -1,451). Falsification: (1) buys after the outcome is decided: false, 89% of profit is from fills before the market's T90, after T99 it earns zero; (2) drift is its own prints: false, with own rows removed the independent price is +3.4 c after 10 minutes, positive in 143 of 149 markets; (3) momentum follower: false, taker fills against a 14 c prior move earn 34% of notional. Not checked: publication times at the sources (Deadline and The Numbers blocked here); phases are inferred from tape jumps.
wallets.replicability: Feasible at small size, hard to do well. Needs a model mapping previews / Friday / estimate to the final 3-day gross (history from Box Office Mojo, reachable), REST polling every few minutes, and $20-50 tickets across 6-12 buckets a weekend. Copying its fills does not work: -1.4 c/share (t = -0.3, 47 markets) at the worst print within 15 minutes, and 39 of 112 signals had no independent print at all. Room: a few hundred dollars per bucket; cat-dog already takes about $11K a month out of the niche. Risks: bucket boundaries, estimate-vs-actual revisions, thin books.

wallets.name: shovelingdigging
wallets.numbers: API monthly kept: May 2,453, Jun -1,388, Jul 10,483, Aug -3,938, Sep 20,056, Oct 22,870, Nov 12,354; rebates 3%. 60 days, 150 of 337 markets (110 resolved): PnL +26,127 on $145K (18%), 80 winners; open positions marked +11,163; total matches API Oct+Nov 35,224 within 6%. Peak capital $47K, 32 markets open at once, about 80-88% taker, sells only 29% of what it buys. By sub-family (resolved): Billboard -1,378 (25 mkts), box office +1,254 (20), Spotify +2,639 (12), album sales +1,224 (10, t 3.2), YouTube views +2,719 (17), next-James-Bond shorts +4,082 (7), non-culture market-cap rank +8,913 (4).
wallets.mechanism: Pop-data generalist. Tracks public running counters (YouTube view counter, Spotify daily charts, HITS Daily Double, The Numbers) and buys buckets 2-10 days before the end when the running number already makes them likely; holds to settlement. Discretionary breadth across about 100 slug families.
wallets.time_gap: Model / data edge with a lag of days, not a latency play. The 6-24 hours-to-end bucket loses (-3,246). Taker fills in quiet markets are followed by +6.3 c on other people's trades within 10 minutes. Fee 0.01.
wallets.evidence: 110 resolved markets; 94% of profit from fills before the market's T90. Falsification: no single sub-family is significant in 60 days and Billboard, its largest by dollars, is negative; a third of resolved profit is two non-culture bets (Apple largest company +4,995, Lula +3,710). Copy test: +8.4 c/share (t = 1.6, 55 markets) but first half +14.1 c, second half -0.9 c. Its other 187 markets were not examined.
wallets.replicability: Partly. Each sub-niche needs its own scraper and bucket model (kworb reachable here; open.spotify.com/charts is not). Capital of a few hundred dollars is enough per niche; median market volume $17K. Following its fills is unstable. Two of the last seven months were negative.

wallets.name: hixlz
wallets.numbers: Joined 2026-10-22. API: Oct +31,628, Nov +8,103, all-time +39,732, rebates under 1%. 35 days, 149 Elon post-count markets, 30 events: +40,530 on $21.4K of buys; 9 winning markets of 127, 8 winning events of 30, event-level t = 1.86, best event +14,256, median event -32. 91% maker, buys only, never sells, median fill $1, median cost per market $26, peak capital $3.0K, up to 39 markets open. Tool 33,638 vs API 36,812 over 30 days: agree.
wallets.mechanism: Long variance in the final post count. Rests bids of 1-15 cents on the bucket just above the pace-projected bucket in the last 6-13 hours and holds to the end. 952 fills in that cell (13 events) cost $8,148 and made +28,604; buckets two or more above pace lost -2,351; 118 losing markets cost $15.2K in total at an average price of 1.9 cents.
wallets.time_gap: None exploited: zero fills in a bucket already dead by arithmetic or after the window. It is a model edge on the spread of the final count. For reference, the official counter lags the post by a median 161 s (p90 296 s). Maker fills, so no fee.
wallets.evidence: Official counter data (xtracker public API) matched the resolved bucket in 21 of 21 events. Winning tickets: 380-399 at 0.060 (13,795 shares, 5-9 h before the end, 42 posts still needed at T-6h with the market at 0.02); 90-114 at 0.133 (17,008 shares); 140-164 at 0.031. Unconditional check on 24 events: the pace projection is off by RMSE 18.7 posts (about one bucket) at T-12h and the eventual winner trades at or below 0.20 in 6 of 24 events. Exploratory, not a fill test: buying the pace bucket at T-12h loses 31 c (t = -3.5, 23 events) while its two neighbours gain 13 c each (t about 1.3).
wallets.replicability: Technically the easiest to copy: free count data, resting bids, tickets of $1-25, $300-3,000 of capital, no speed. But the evidence is two months, one account and eight winning events; 22 of 30 events lose and the result depends on a few 10-30x hits. Median market volume $86K, so size is not the limit; competition for the same cheap bids is.

wallets.name: Elonurmom
wallets.numbers: API monthly kept, last 12: +403, +2,004, -3,557, +10,687, +3,257, +8,312, -10,939, +403, -2,537, +2,168, +8,383, +4,874 (8 of 12 positive; all-time +15.5K). 60 days, 120 of 190 markets, 17 events: +2,605 on $133K (2.0%), 10 winning events, t = 0.27, worst event -7,617; open positions +5,874. 96% taker, sells 8% of buys, median market buy $400, up to $3,000, peak capital $25K. Tool vs API reconciles only 64% (70 markets left out, 7 conversions not modelled).
wallets.mechanism: Early (2-7 days out) taker bets that the final count lands below the current pace, held to the end. Buckets two or more below pace: +7,350 on $51.6K (13 events); on-pace bucket -3,652; one above -3,016; last six hours -7,495.
wallets.time_gap: None found. Independent price after its fills is -0.5 c at 10 minutes. Model edge at best. Fee 0.01.
wallets.evidence: 17 events, counter data matched resolutions in 15 of 15 usable events. Falsification of 'it has an information lead': price does not follow its fills, and its late trades lose. The positive expectancy is not distinguishable from zero in this window; the monthly record carries the case.
wallets.replicability: Anyone can place these bets; there is no demonstrated edge to copy. Needs $400-3,000 per bucket to matter and tolerates -$10K months.

wallets.name: ayosussybenny
wallets.numbers: API monthly kept: Aug 2,313, Sep 1,139, Oct 2,663, Nov 7,191; volume $13-33K a month; rebates 1%; 98% taker. 90 days, 150 of 353 markets: streamer deadline markets 43 markets / 28 events, +9,041 on $25.2K, 18 winning events, t = 1.59, best event +5,074; sports 87 markets +508 on $21.5K (t = 0.24). Peak capital $2.8K, median market buy $210. Tool 7,134 vs API 7,943 over 14 days: agree.
wallets.mechanism: Watches the live stream that resolves the market (Kai Cenat, xQc, IShowSpeed 'finish GTA VI by date') and prices remaining playtime against the deadline better than the crowd; trades several date markets in a 15-minute burst.
wallets.time_gap: Hours, and attention rather than latency: +0.3 c at 10 minutes after its fills, +6.8 c at 24 hours. The stream state is public but nobody aggregates it. Fee 0.01.

analysis.patterns:
What the culture winners have in common (seven accounts, about 760 market tapes):

1. One source, one model. Each specialist owns a single public data source and a way to turn its running value into bucket probabilities: The Numbers / trade-press box office (cat-dog), the xtracker post counter (hixlz, Elonurmom), a live stream (ayosussybenny, Electricy), view and chart counters (shovelingdigging). None is a generalist in the profitable part of its book; ayosussybenny's 87 sports markets earn nothing.

2. They trade before the market is decided. Share of resolved profit from fills before the market's own T90: cat-dog 89%, shovelingdigging 94%, ayosussybenny 100%, hixlz all of it. "Buy after the deciding observation" is not where the money is.

3. The time gap is an overshoot, not a delay. In box office the crowd reacts to each number within the half hour and goes too far: following a 10-cent jump loses 9.7 c/share (t = -2.3, 50 markets, selected sample). The winners fade it and wait for the next number.

4. The crowd is over-confident about the central bucket. Elon events, 24 unconditional: at T-12h the pace projection is still off by about one bucket (RMSE 18.7 posts) yet the pace bucket costs 0.53 on average and hits 5 of 23; the eventual winner is at or below 0.20 in 6 of 24 events. Same shape in box office when a studio estimate sits near a boundary.

5. Takers who move the price, and cannot be followed. cat-dog and shovelingdigging are 57-88% taker; other people's prices move 6-7 c within 10 minutes of their taker fills. Copying cat-dog at the worst print within 15 minutes earns -1.4 c (t = -0.3); about 40% of signals have no print to copy at all.

6. Hold to settlement, small tickets, many buckets. Median buy per market $26-624, 8-32 markets open at once, sells are mostly winners unloaded at 0.999. Fee at 0.01 is at most 0.25 c a share and does not matter to any of them; rebates are 1-3% of what they keep.

7. A near-certain carry leg exists: buys at 0.90-0.995 earned 2.6-4.4% per turn over about 4.5 days for cat-dog (50 markets, no loser) and shovelingdigging (25 markets, 2 losers); Electricy and Elonurmom each took one loss of $2-3K that ate the leg.

8. Board hygiene: three leaders are artefacts or unverifiable (anothercoin, 0xc023bee9, pleaseletmealone), all conversion users. Markets are thin: median volume $13-17K per box-office or chart bucket, $86-180K per Elon bucket.

Negative results recorded: copy rule (2 variants x 2 accounts), jump-follow (1 variant), 12 exploratory Elon bucket variants of which one stands out and none is a fill test. Not verified: source publication times for box office, stream state, any order-book depth.

The 14-day `pmlab.wallet` runs were made as asked (none truncated), but they are of little use here: tool totals were 8-80% of the API's for the same days, because these markets have end dates months away, resolve early, and most PnL sits in carried-in, merged or still-open markets.
