wallets.name: fountaim
wallets.numbers: 88 days: kept 12,336 on $37,837 volume (32%), 236 fills, 175 markets, 98-100% taker, 99% buys, rebates 0%. Positive in all 7 months since May (Sep +4.9K, Oct +3.2K, Nov +4.3K). One fill of $300-1,100 per market, held to settlement. Fee paid about 0.76 c/share against about 20 c of edge.
wallets.mechanism: Leaderboard sniper. When a model's row first appears on arena.ai or the HLE page, it buys the decided side on every sibling threshold in the same second while the book is still at the old prices. It uses the same reflex on arena-score milestone markets, month-end rank legs after a rank change, and private-company valuation markets after funding news.
wallets.time_gap: Source: the arena.ai Text Arena leaderboard and agi.safe.ai (HLE-Diamond). The market rule checks the value at 12:00 ET the day after first appearance, so far thresholds are decided the moment the row appears. The lag between traders is 0-2 s: in all 15 of its sweeps another wallet bought the same winner in the same block. The lag from the leaderboard update to the first trade could not be measured (no archive of the page).
wallets.evidence: 32 late debut fills in 32 markets, 32 on the right side. The bought side was at 0.668 on the tape 10 s before, it paid 0.785, the tape was at 0.973 ten minutes later; 26 of 32 fills are within 5 s of the first trade of the burst; net $5.0K after fees. Kimi K3.1 Pro, Nov 9 19:54:33 UTC: bought No on three score thresholds and the top-20 rank market in one second at 0.75-0.91, all won (+$527). Gemini Carbon HLE >=65%, Nov 12 00:35: bought No at 0.234 while Yes stood near 0.9, 24 minutes before the rest moved (+$1,984). Falsification (right side and price jump after the fill) held 32 of 32 and 26 of 32. Its buys below 0.80 in all resolved tech markets win 87-92% (60 markets).
wallets.replicability: Needs a poller on arena.ai and agi.safe.ai with second-level detection, a parser that maps a new row to every sibling threshold, and pre-signed orders; capital of $300-1,000 per market is enough. But 85% of the gap money ($12.0K of $14.1K over 20 events in 12 weeks) is taken within 3 s by 68 wallets, so a one-server newcomer competes for a share of about $1K a week against at least three faster bots. Risks: the score drifting across a near threshold before the noon check, name-matching rules (which model qualifies), AutoEval rows, and the Nex exchange in mid-December shrinking the window further.

Astra, Sep 11 21:18:10: bought No at 0.537 one second after the first print and sold at 0.95 as a maker 16 minutes later. Month-end legs: 15 taker buys more than a day before the check, 76-100% right, net about $6.4K over 13 markets, of which $4.4K is one event (best AI model end of October). Pre-appearance sells lost about $3.7K. Top 3 events are $6.4K of its $7.2K arena net over 30 events. Falsification of 'sniper': 73% of its 15 late debut buys lead the burst, 93% right.

wallets.name: KimchiCapital
wallets.numbers: 88 days: kept 36,487 on $316,790 volume, 2,199 fills, 897 markets, 59% tech, 85-97% taker, rebates 2%. Positive every month since January (Sep +10.9K, Oct +9.3K, Nov +16.3K). About $145 per fill, up to $5.4K on single late entries.

It does the same in IPO/valuation, release-date, OpenRouter-share, finance and culture markets; arena and HLE are a small part of its profit.

Late debut buys: 18 fills, 18 right, tape 0.851 before, fill 0.861, 0.877 ten minutes later, so it is not the one moving the price (only half lead a burst), which falsifies 'sniper'. Mistral Large 4 >=1490: No at 0.930 for $4,901, 55 s after the sweep. Fable 5.2 HLE >=70%: Yes at 0.943 for $5,377, 16 h before the check. But the edge is selecting which favourites are safe, and one wrong 0.93 buy costs 13 right ones. My pre-registered follower rule on the same idea was 17 for 17 in 9 events, which cannot rule out a loss rate below about 16%.

wallets.numbers: 88 days: kept 63,442 on $407,740 volume, 2,203 fills, 330 markets, 95% tech, 90-95% taker, rebates 3%. 10 of 11 months positive, but Nov +43.3K against Sep +10.9K and Oct +9.2K. About $185 per fill, up to $29.6K turnover in one event.

analysis.patterns:
1. The money in tech that is systematic sits in leaderboard markets. "Debut" markets resolve on the arena.ai or HLE value at 12:00 ET the day after the model's row first appears, so the deciding number is public 12-36 hours before the check.

2. That gap is real but already a race. Over 20 debut events in 12 weeks (279 whole-market tapes), takers who bought the eventual winner below 0.97 took $14.1K in total; 85% of it went within 3 seconds of the first print, to 68 wallets. Every sweep by the two snipers I studied had another buyer in the same block. The leaderboard operator's X posts come hours later (once after the check itself), so the snipers read the page, not the feed.

3. What is left after the first seconds is small but positive: about 5-7 cents a share on roughly $33K of buying over 12 weeks. Ten minutes after a sweep, no sibling market was priced at 0.90 or more on the wrong side (0 of 77), which bounds the reversal rate at about 5%, the same size as the discount.

4. Winners are takers, not makers: 82-100% taker share in tech for six of the seven, rebate share 0-12% (NoTeacher 24%). They accept the 0.05 fee because the edge per share is 5-30 cents.

5. Three distinct ways of winning appear, in order of how much speed they need:
- sniping the leaderboard row (fountaim, part of lamyk): seconds, 100% hit rate, small capital;
- buying near-decided favourites at 0.80-0.95 minutes to hours later (KimchiCapital): 97-100% hit rate on 58-73 markets per bucket;
- forecasting where a model will land days ahead (iutwpfal, NoTeacher) or pricing month-end ranks across a thousand legs (0xAee8611B): no speed, a model edge.

6. The largest results are concentrated: iutwpfal's top 3 events are 75% of its arena profit and November is 68% of its quarter. Only 0xAee8611B and fountaim have results spread over many events.

7. Bonds do not pay: melonmanm's $163K of tech buys at 0.95+ grossed $232, and NoTeacher's 0.98+ buys won only 92%.

8. Holding to settlement is the norm, and exits are often made by buying the opposite side and merging rather than selling.

wallets.name: Bigggggggg
wallets.numbers: API economic PnL +534.3K (first on the politics month board at 2.13M). Rebuilt from cash since 2026-05-16: bought $17.66M, conversions $16.08M, sells $1.10M, merges $0.52M, rewards and rebates $47.2K; net cash +$108.1K plus $4.4K of open positions = +$112.5K real, of which trading +$65.3K. Last 14 days: 9,668 fills, all neg-risk; BUY No $883K (75% taker), SELL Yes $96K (74% maker); 124 events with conversions; 64% of NO dollars bought at 0.90 or higher.
wallets.mechanism: Structural neg-risk trade. It buys equal NO share counts (8-9K) on the 10-15 leading outcomes of events with 22-128 outcomes, converts the m NO legs into m-1 USDC plus one YES of every other outcome, then sells that tail of longshot YES as a maker. Cash returns in the conversion; the worst case per set is the basket shortfall of a few cents.
wallets.time_gap: None. It is a structural edge: YES prices of large multi-outcome events sum above 1, and conversion lets the buyer of the leaders' NO own the tail for free or better. No information lag is involved.
wallets.evidence: Six largest events of the window, basket cost against payout m-1: +4.7c, +5.1c, +15.9c, -10.3c, -4.3c, +2.0c per set before fees, with tail YES sold for $0-3.5K each. Falsification at event level over the whole life: 1,400 conversion events, +$71.2K = +0.41% of buys, t 4.3 by event, 64% positive. Its 192 non-conversion events lose 5.1% (t -1.2). The mechanism survives; the board figure does not.
wallets.replicability: Needs live books for every leg of every large neg-risk event, the conversion call, and resting sells on 100+ tail legs. Its sets are about $100K; a minimum 5-share set of 12 legs costs about $55 for a margin of cents. Fee is the category taker rate on NO legs (0.05 elections, 0.01 other politics; about 0.1c a leg at 0.98). The smaller copies all lose on the trade (kaxel78 -0.31%, glpgb -0.84%, VerilyWinningly -2.07% of buys), at least nine accounts on the board do it, and the API shows November negative for this account (not rebuilt by month). Capacity is about $90K a day of turnover for roughly $330 a day of trading result.

wallets.name: Car
wallets.numbers: All time kept $1.69M on $119M (+1.42% of volume), rebates and rewards 6%, Tier 0. Positive in 27 of the last 30 months; Sep/Oct/Nov 2026 +32.3K/+35.8K/+45.2K. No conversions; tool and API agree for the 14 days (6.5K vs 8.0K). Politics, 30 days: 2,687 fills, $511K, 106 markets in 54 events, 49% taker, median fill $17, p99 $2,369.
wallets.mechanism: Informed two-sided trader of geopolitics and by-date news markets (US x Iran ceasefire and blockade ladders, Hegseth out, FAA ground stop, Trump meetings). It takes aggressively when it knows something and rests orders otherwise. It both exits (36% of buys round-tripped at +1.42c; median hold about 2 days) and holds to settlement.
wallets.time_gap: Partly seconds after a headline in fee-free geopolitics markets: its first fill came 0-5 s after the first print of the move in 9 of 12 sampled stories. Mostly it is an information and rule-knowledge edge. The public timestamp of each headline was not obtained, so lags are from the first print, not from the news.
wallets.evidence: Mark-outs on 40 markets, clustered by market: taker buys +1.34c after 1 min (t 4.3) and +1.76c after 10 min (t 3.2); maker buys +1.0c after 10 min (t 3.2) and +1.5c after a day (t 5.2), so its resting orders are not adversely selected. Example: Iran ceasefire by Nov 15, YES 0.31 to 0.03 on 17 Nov 19:19:46 UTC; it took 24,320 NO at 0.917 one second later and held to resolution about 2 h later. A loss is in the sample too (sold Trump-Putin YES at 0.602, resolved YES, about -$1.2K). Falsification of 'first-second news bot': a fill within 10 s in only 14 of 394 jumps, worth $4.2K of 5-minute value against a month of $45K. That claim fails as the main mechanism.
wallets.replicability: Needs a news feed faster than the crowd for US/Iran/Russia and cabinet items, reaction in 1-5 s, close reading of rule text, and $10-30K per event. Fee is 0 on geopolitics (gamma feeType None) and 0.01 on other politics. Its entries are 2-25K shares in markets with $0.1-3.3M of volume. The informed part is not copyable by us; following its fills is a testable idea.

wallets.name: Cb94C437
wallets.numbers: Joined 2026-06-22. All time: gross +$338.0K (+1.32% of $25.56M), taker fees -$148.6K, taker rebates +$30.7K, kept $220.1K. Kept Jun-Nov: 30.2K/91.1K/19.5K/29.2K/19.2K/30.9K. For the rest, no price move in its own or a sibling market precedes the buy, so the signal is something not visible on the tape. It is not a headline reactor: a fill within 10 s in 28 of 380 jumps.

Only 31% of buys follow a same-direction print in the prior 30 s. Pre-registered T2: sibling moved before 22.2% of 1,638 buys against 9.0% at placebo times (ratio 2.48, prediction met). Falsification of 'maker in disguise': 0 maker fills of 35,346 and $21 of maker rebate in five months. Rebates are 14% of what it kept.

It paid 0.58% of volume in fees under the old 0.04-0.05 rates; fees were 62% of its November gross. The cut to 0.01 since Nov 21 helps this style most. Typical clip is $7-90.

wallets.name: 0x9495d622
wallets.numbers: 14 days: 12,006 fills in 2,963 markets, 97% maker, median market turnover $12; trade PnL -12.8K, rewards +21.2K, kept +9.2K. Monthly Jun-Nov: gross -12.4K/-26.6K/-11.5K/-3.2K/-28.7K/-33.0K, rewards and rebates +17.3K/+34.8K/+16.2K/+11.8K/+47.3K/+47.5K, kept +4.6K/+7.6K/+4.7K/+8.4K/+18.4K/+14.2K. 60 days of cash: rewards $91.5K, maker rebates $4.2K, net cash +$9.2K. analysis.patterns:
1. The politics board cannot be read at face value. Every account with neg-risk conversions is overstated by the API: Bigggggggg 534K against 112K real, kaxel78 81K against 5.5K, glpgb 90K against -1K, VerilyWinningly 37K against -1K, BetaShrimp 8.9K against 1.7K. `tools/leaders.py` and `pmlab.wallet` inherit the problem; `cash.py` and `evstats.py` in the study folder rebuild the result from activity rows.

2. Real, persistent profit comes from three sources, none of them speed alone:
- Structure: the neg-risk conversion trade, which pays only at Bigggggggg's size (+0.41% of buys, t 4.3 over 1,400 events) and loses for three smaller copies.
- Subject knowledge in fee-free geopolitics: Car, positive 27 of 30 months, with positive mark-outs on both its taker and its maker fills.
- One pure taker with a short-horizon signal: Cb94C437, six of six months positive, +1.32% gross on $25.6M, median hold 54 minutes.

3. Reward farming is real but thin. Three makers lose on every fill (maker buys are 0.8c under water a minute later) and keep between a tenth and a half of the rewards. The makers who also earn the spread (Lolakis, Car) quote about 50 markets in size, not hundreds at the minimum.

4. Nobody in the sample systematically buys at 0.95 and above in politics. The blanket rule shows no edge on 24 resolved tapes: -0.48c a share after fee, t -0.2, with buyers on the losing side in 6 of 24 markets. This was pre-registered with one variant, on a small and selected sample.

5. Fees decide the taker style. Cb94C437 gave 44% of its lifetime gross to fees under the old 0.04-0.05 rates. Geopolitics is 0 and other politics is 0.01 since Nov 21.

6. Time gaps seen but not proven:
- Sibling legs of one event reprice with a lag: median 12 s, p90 133 s, over 52 follower legs in 12 events. $3.1K of the $3.75K of stale-print value comes from one FAA leg.
- A dead leg of a geopolitics ladder still traded at 0.917 one second after the disqualifying event and at 0.989-0.99 for two more hours at zero fee (one event).

Limits: the public timestamp of each headline was not obtained; no historical book depth was used; most accounts have 14 days of fills; monthly persistence is reliable only for accounts without conversions; I did not rebuild xtxpleasecallme or the 0x9b129aD0 cluster.

I also appended the verified facts to /home/user/polymarket-lab/NOTES.md. The protocol for the two pre-registered tests is /home/user/polymarket-lab/studies/wallets/politics/protocol.md; it was written before those two tests but after the descriptive work.
